title: Art Tatum the pinochle player
summary: Tatum loved pinochle and held cards close to his good eye; Stewart and guitarists played with him for fun.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: What are the things that you recall about him as a person, other than his playing the piano?

Well, he was quite a fellow. We used to -- one thing that kind of sticks out in my mind, how he loved to play cards. And he and I and a couple of our friends would get together and get into a card game, and Art Tatum's specialty was pinochle.

Yes. Now, in the first place, people -- folks would ask me how in the world could he play cards, and he couldn't see. Well, anyway, this is possibly the way he got around that. He wasn't totally blind. He could see out of one eye possibly -- he had to see visions of some sort, you know, where he could possibly make out the cards. He would put the card up to his good eye where he could possibly see a little bit, put it right up to his eye, and he -- no doubt he was making out what that card was.
Would he put it as close as you just put your hand almost like if you had a compress on his eye?
Yes, very close, yes. And just the way he got around it. And we used to -- every chance we got -- play this pinochle, and he won, but he was, in other words, he considered himself to be a champ.
Did you all play for money?
Well, not really, just what do you say -- no, we didn't pay, just play for the fun of it, you know.
Did you -- who were some of the other guys that you remember who liked the cards?

Well, of course, guitarists like Tiny, Tiny used to play with us, and Everett Barksdale, he was with us at one time, John Collins. And quite a few other musicians at times when we were at one or the other's house, you know, had a little party or something, you know, start playing cards, because that was, oh, Art Tatum's favorite sport-like, you might say.
